clue.text: Deposit a ball tackling five

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to tackle something is to get hold of it, so the ball wraps itself around the number

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A footballer seems to be putting the ball down while tackling five opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' looks like the football in the scene, but it is the formal party with music.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is money paid up front before the rest is due, much like a deposit.

clue.text: Ships notice a weapon ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the weapon at the front, before the other words

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
an ad is a notice in a paper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lookouts spot a ship's weapon ahead, a naval warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Go a bit like a van?

parts.note: the vehicle, taken as written
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is moving off a little like being a van?
explanation.walkthrough: Something a bit like a van would be van-ish; split it differently and it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to disappear, and go can mean to disappear or cease to exist.

clue.text: Fussy pink gin and tonic cocktail not on!

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together
not on tells you to remove those two letters from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy drinker declares a pink gin and tonic cocktail just not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: TONIC loses its ON to leave TIC, which joins PINK GIN in the mix. 'Not on' is also British for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitpicking is excessive concern with trivial details, the behaviour of someone fussy.

clue.text: Nurse finally backing the last word in 'help to go'

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of nurse

indicators.note: backing makes the phrase that follows run from back to front

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

explanation.surface: A nurse gets the final say on what helps a patient move along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help to go' is a coy hint at what the procedure does for the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema flushes the lower bowel, a medical aid for constipation, coyly described here.

clue.text: Delight in French tea — firstly need teapot!

parts.note: en is French for in
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: firstly asks for the opening letter of each of the two words that follow it

parts.note: opening letter of need
opening letter of teapot

explanation.surface: A tea lover in France is thrilled, but first of all needs a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm and please them greatly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Her Majesty embraces coastal regeneration — this can go up and down

definitions.text: this can go up and down

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

indicators.note: regeneration rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The Queen welcomes the revival of a seaside town, whose fortunes go up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit between E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries shoppers upward or downward, so this definition describes it whimsically.

clue.text: Talk fondly, reportedly upset

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken by others, so we go by the sound of a word

parts.note: to coo is to murmur softly and lovingly

explanation.surface: Someone who talks lovingly is said to be upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of the French loanword is silent, so it sounds just like the dove's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden overthrow of a government, a political upset.

clue.text: Playing sitar, go for creative talent

indicators.note: playing with the letters means arranging them a different way

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A music teacher urges trying the sitar to show creative flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is skill in an art, the creative ability shown by a gifted maker or performer.

clue.text: Go blue in decline

parts.note: to go sour is to turn sour; both mean become
feeling blue is feeling down, sad

explanation.surface: Someone becomes depressed as their health or fortunes slide.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to refuse or reject an offer, a straight synonym of the verb decline.

clue.text: Painter's second bag

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time like a second
to net something is to bag or catch it

explanation.surface: Reads like an inventory of an artist's belongings: his second bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the painter to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the water lilies series.

clue.text: Come across 'im calculating number of chickens?

indicators.note: writing him as 'im shows a speaker who drops their aitches, so the next word loses its H too

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
someone who calculates the number of things is a counter

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether some fellow is busy totting up his chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen counter, said by someone who drops their H the way they say 'im, becomes 'en counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter something is to meet it by chance, which is what come across means.

clue.text: Paid celebs can be loathsome

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters could be made into something else when rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sour comment that celebrities who take payment can be thoroughly hateful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something despicable deserves contempt and disgust, the same feeling captured by loathsome.

clue.text: Unhappy start to song and dance

indicators.note: the start of each word that follows is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of song
first letter of and
first letter of dance

explanation.surface: A song and dance act opens on a gloomy note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' applies to all three words, not just song.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad and unhappy are plain synonyms for being in low spirits or sorrowful.

clue.text: Get lost cycling

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British phrase telling someone to go away
second meaning: literally, riding a bicycle

explanation.walkthrough: The British dismissal, telling someone to clear off, is read literally as being in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for go away, and literally describes someone riding a bicycle.

clue.text: 27s knew about minimum staff

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a fresh order

parts.note: 27 across is voter; the plural of that entry's word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Voters knew all about the bare minimum staffing in some public service.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 27s means the answer to 27 across with an S added.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton crew is the smallest number of workers needed to keep an operation running.

clue.text: Speech interpreter repaired learner's translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a different form, so the letters change their order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A learner's translation has been corrected by an interpreter.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person who reads mouth movements interprets speech visually without hearing it.

clue.text: Suck like Blackbeard?

parts.note: as means in the manner of
Blackbeard was the notorious 18th-century pirate Edward Teach

explanation.surface: A question whether sucking is typical of the famous buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Blackbeard is an example of a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate is to draw fluid out by suction, as a doctor does with a syringe.

clue.text: Plaudit for a cold soft drink extremely desirable

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
cola is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the two end letters of the word after

parts.note: outer letters of desirable

explanation.surface: Praise for a chilled soft drink that is wonderfully desirable, like an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, the same as a plaudit.

clue.text: You could be Eve

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the grammatical person used for the one addressed
second meaning: in Genesis she was created after Adam, so she came next in line

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a remark that you might be Eve; really you is a grammar term and Eve was the Bible's number two human. Both definitions are examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls the pronoun you this form, and Eve was the second human created after Adam.

clue.text: Be able to send up small amount of food?

parts.note: can means be able to
to ape is to mimic, to send someone up

explanation.surface: Someone is able to send a little food up to a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' looks like a reversal signal but means mock or imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served on bread or a cracker at parties.

clue.text: Realise Jeff's topless, hairy etc

indicators.note: topless means without the top, which in a down clue is the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: hairy means dodgy or wild, so the following letters are in disorder

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of Jeff stripped to the waist, chest hair and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'hairy' both look like descriptions of Jeff; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect a change is to bring it about, which is one sense of realise, as in realising a plan.

clue.text: They say that in marriage libido is reduced by 50% …

indicators.note: cutting something by half throws away its first three of six letters here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry observation that married couples find their sex drive halved.
explanation.walkthrough: The front half is dropped, leaving the back half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The bride and groom each say these words during the wedding vows to accept one another.

clue.text: … to improve share for partner?

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
a half is a share of something

explanation.surface: Continuing the marriage theme: a halved libido might be improved by sharing with a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a jokey idiom for one's husband or wife, a life partner.

clue.text: Herb for porridge, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word and listen to its sound

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, time inside

explanation.surface: A breakfast tip: a herb to flavour porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is not the oat dish but slang for a jail term, as in doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a fragrant culinary herb of the mint family.

clue.text: One shared by community with opportunities

indicators.note: shared by means held in common within the word that follows, its letters sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A single place shared by a thriving community full of opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With opportunities' only extends the surface picture of the community.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single whole thing, and the number one is also called unity or a unit.

clue.text: On which one gets wet, save for this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a day of showers
second meaning: the idiom about putting money aside for hard times

explanation.walkthrough: The second half completes a well-known saying, putting money by for a time of need.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a day with showers soaks you, and idiomatically one saves money for a future emergency of that name.

clue.text: Playing a nine is stupid

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them around into another order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A golfer's or card player's choice to play a nine is judged foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes something silly, senseless or lacking intelligence, matching stupid.

clue.text: Voter getting shock treatment in role reversal

indicators.note: in places the treatment inside the other word
a reversal turns the word role back to front, letter by letter

parts.note: taken as written
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a psychiatric shock treatment

explanation.surface: A voter given electric shocks as part of a role-swap game, a strange political drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Role reversal' looks like a stock phrase, but it tells you to read the word role backwards; ECT is electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a person entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Peak at any time east of Paris

parts.note: ever means at any time
est is French for east, the language of Paris

explanation.surface: Something sits east of Paris, at whatever time of day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of Paris' flags a French word rather than a place east of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest in the Himalayas is the highest mountain summit on Earth.
